data.title: RAFT1 phosphorylation of the translational regulators p70 S6 kinase and 4E-BP1
data.authors: Burnett PE; Sabatini DM et al.
data.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: RAFT1/mTOR directly phosphorylates p70 S6K (Thr389) and 4E-BP1, the two central translational effectors.
data.abstract_excerpt: The complex of rapamycin with its intracellular receptor, FKBP12, interacts with RAFT1/FRAP/mTOR, the in vivo rapamycin-sensitive target and a member of the ataxia telangiectasia mutated (ATM)-related family of kinases that share homology with the catalytic domain of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase. The function of RAFT1 in the rapamycin-sensitive pathway and its connection to downstream components of the pathway, such as p70 S6 kinase and 4E-BP1, are poorly understood.

extracted_findings.effect: RAFT1/mTOR directly phosphorylates p70 S6K and 4E-BP1 – connects mTOR to translational regulators
